identity.title: Severe postural dizziness / inability to stand for vitals

technique.how: After 2 minutes supine, have the patient stand (with assistance) and ask about dizziness while measuring pulse and BP at about 1 minute. Record 'severe postural dizziness' when the patient cannot stand long enough for upright vitals because of lightheadedness or near-syncope; also record the supine-to-standing pulse increment.
technique.prerequisites: Patient can safely attempt standing with an assistant; supine baseline vitals obtained first.
technique.contraindications: Do not attempt standing in patients who are hypotensive supine, acutely bleeding with instability, or at high fall risk without assistance.

interpretation.positive_finding: Severe postural dizziness (or a postural pulse increment of 30/min or more) has sensitivity 0.97 and specificity 0.98 for large acute blood loss, so its presence strongly supports significant hypovolemia.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence does not exclude moderate blood loss (sensitivity only 0.22 after ~450-630 mL); supine hypotension and tachycardia are also frequently absent.
interpretation.pitfalls: Mild postural dizziness has no proven diagnostic value. Data come from phlebotomised healthy volunteers, not ED patients with vomiting/diarrhoea, where few findings have proven utility; beta-blockers, autonomic neuropathy, and deconditioning confound.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as significant volume/blood loss - IV access, fluids or blood, search for bleeding. Negative: does not rule out moderate loss; check haemoglobin, BUN/creatinine, electrolytes.

estimates.target_condition: Large acute blood loss (phlebotomy of larger volumes, up to 1150 mL) - finding: severe postural dizziness (unable to stand for upright vitals) OR postural pulse increment >=30/min
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing phlebotomy (pooled from studies of postural vital signs)
estimates.reference_standard: Known volume of blood removed by phlebotomy
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.97/(1-0.98) = 48.5; LR- = (1-0.97)/0.98 = 0.03; from abstract sensitivity 97% and specificity 98%
estimates.quote: a much greater sensitivity for large blood loss of 97% (95% CI, 91%-100%); the corresponding specificity is 98% (95% CI, 97%-99%)

estimates.target_condition: Moderate acute blood loss (e.g. 450 mL phlebotomy) - finding: severe postural dizziness OR postural pulse increment >=30/min
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing phlebotomy (pooled; includes Witting 1994, 345 blood donors, 450 mL)
estimates.reference_standard: Known volume of blood removed by phlebotomy
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.22/(1-0.98) = 11.0; LR- = (1-0.22)/0.98 = 0.80; from abstract sensitivity 22% and specificity 98%
estimates.quote: The presence of either finding has a sensitivity for moderate blood loss of only 22% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6%-48%)

sources.citation: McGee S, Abernethy WB 3rd, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA. 1999;281(11):1022-1029.
Witting MD, Wears RL, Li S. Defining the positive tilt test: a study of healthy adults with moderate acute blood loss. Ann Emerg Med. 1994;23(6):1320-1323.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not stand a patient who is already hypotensive or unstable; do not apply the volunteer-derived numbers directly to elderly patients with vomiting/diarrhoea, autonomic failure, or on rate-limiting drugs.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Inability to stand from dizziness after suspected bleeding signals large-volume loss - activate haemorrhage management rather than waiting for supine hypotension.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Defined operationally as inability to stand for vitals, which is more reproducible than graded dizziness; the RCE notes mild postural dizziness has no proven value.

extraction_notes: Both estimates are verbatim from the 1999 RCE abstract (PMID 10086438, confirmed) and refer to the COMBINED finding 'severe postural dizziness (preventing upright vitals) OR postural pulse increment >=30/min', not severe dizziness alone; the abstract does not report severe dizziness in isolation and the JAMA table is not open-access. LRs are computed from the abstract sens/spec (no CIs). Blood-loss volume categories (moderate vs large) are the review's own; exact mL cut-offs are not stated in the abstract, so they are described approximately (included studies phlebotomised up to 1150 mL; Witting 1994 used 450 mL). Witting 1994 (PMID 8198307, confirmed) abstract reports no sens/spec figures, so it is cited as the primary cohort only. Setting coded 'outpatient' because subjects were volunteer blood donors, not patients.
